      "observed": "All VDD pins of both MCUs (FCC2 pins 11, 27, 50, 75, 100; NAVC2 pins 19, 32, 48, 64) are on no-connect nets. The rail that carries the MCU-side connectors and decoupling (+3V3) has no source. The LDO output (REG3 pin 1 OUT) sits on a separate net, +3.3V, which does not connect to +3V3.",
      "expected": "Both MCU VDD pins should be tied to the regulated 3V3 rail, and the LDO output should reach the MCU supply net. The spec says the 3V3 rail feeds both MCUs.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"1\") (name \"+3.3V\")"},

        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"216\") (name \"unconnected-(FCC2-VDD-Pad11)\")"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs"}
      ],
      "impact": "Neither MCU would receive supply power from the 3.3 V LDO, so the flight controller and navigation computer would not boot.",
      "confidence": 0.45
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_component_type",
      "components": ["FCC2", "R5", "C78", "C10"],
      "pins": ["FCC2.13", "FCC2.20", "FCC2.21"],
      "nets": ["VREF+_FCC", "VDDA_FCC"],
      "observed": "The analogue reference/supply filter (R5 47 Ω, C78 100 nF, C10 100 nF) lands on FCC2 pin 13, which the library names PH1 (an oscillator pin). FCC2 pin 20 (VREF+) and pin 21 (VDDA) are on no-connect nets.",
      "expected": "On the STM32H753 LQFP-100 the VREF+ and VDDA supply pins should be on the analogue filter network. PH1 is an HSE oscillator pin and should not carry the analogue supply.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"165\") (name \"VREF+_FCC\") (class \"Default\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"FCC2\") (pin \"13\") (pinfunction \"PH1\") (pintype \"bidirectional\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"222\") (name \"unconnected-(FCC2-VREF+-Pad20)\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"221\") (name \"unconnected-(FCC2-VDDA-Pad21)\")"}
      ],
      "impact": "The FCC's ADC reference and analogue supply are not connected where they should be, and the filter node is tied to an oscillator pin. ADC readings (current/voltage sense path, etc.) would be wrong or the clock path disturbed.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["U19"],
      "pins": ["U19.1", "U19.2"],
      "nets": ["+3.3V", "GND"],
      "observed": "PCA9685PW address pin A0 (pin 1) is tied to +3.3V and A1 (pin 2) to GND, so the device address resolves to 0x41, not 0x40. Both A2–A5 are tied to GND.",
      "expected": "The spec lists the PCA9685PW at I2C address 0x40, which requires A0 to be tied to GND.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U19\") (pin \"1\") (pinfunction \"A0\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the spec address is correct, the firmware will not find the PWM driver at 0x40 and servo output will fail. If the 0x41 strap was deliberate to avoid a clash with INA219 at 0x40, the spec is simply out of date.",
      "confidence": 0.2
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The netlist shows both MCU VDD pins unconnected, with the MCU-side 3V3 rail isolated from the LDO output, which contradicts the spec's power architecture. A second likely error is the analogue VREF+/VDDA filter landing on oscillator pin PH1 on the FCC. Both findings rest on the netlist, though the wider netlist sparsity makes the first less certain."
}

anomalies.observed: All VDD pins of both MCUs (FCC2 pins 11, 27, 50, 75, 100; NAVC2 pins 19, 32, 48, 64) are on no-connect nets. The rail that carries the MCU-side connectors and decoupling (+3V3) has no source. The LDO output (REG3 pin 1 OUT) sits on a separate net, +3.3V, which does not connect to +3V3.
anomalies.expected: Both MCU VDD pins should be tied to the regulated 3V3 rail, and the LDO output should reach the MCU supply net. The spec says the 3V3 rail feeds both MCUs.

evidence.quote: 3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs

anomalies.impact: Neither MCU would receive supply power from the 3.3 V LDO, so the flight controller and navigation computer would not boot.

anomalies.observed: The analogue reference/supply filter (R5 47 Ω, C78 100 nF, C10 100 nF) lands on FCC2 pin 13, which the library names PH1 (an oscillator pin). FCC2 pin 20 (VREF+) and pin 21 (VDDA) are on no-connect nets.
anomalies.expected: On the STM32H753 LQFP-100 the VREF+ and VDDA supply pins should be on the analogue filter network. PH1 is an HSE oscillator pin and should not carry the analogue supply.
anomalies.impact: The FCC's ADC reference and analogue supply are not connected where they should be, and the filter node is tied to an oscillator pin. ADC readings (current/voltage sense path, etc.) would be wrong or the clock path disturbed.

anomalies.observed: PCA9685PW address pin A0 (pin 1) is tied to +3.3V and A1 (pin 2) to GND, so the device address resolves to 0x41, not 0x40. Both A2–A5 are tied to GND.
anomalies.expected: The spec lists the PCA9685PW at I2C address 0x40, which requires A0 to be tied to GND.
anomalies.impact: If the spec address is correct, the firmware will not find the PWM driver at 0x40 and servo output will fail. If the 0x41 strap was deliberate to avoid a clash with INA219 at 0x40, the spec is simply out of date.
